location: Hazelwood North, Victoria; proposed US and Malaysian options
status: ASX-listed developer. FY2026 report describes MgO demonstration and a metal circuit under installation, with first plant metal targeted for H2 2026. No sustained commercial metal annual output verified.
feedstock: Demonstration: EnergyAustralia Yallourn brown-coal ash, purchased under amended supply arrangements. Screening, drying and consistency matter; wet/variable ash disrupted initial operation. Raw ash Mg assay not verified. US option: Société Le Nickel (Eramet) ferronickel slag, stated ~33% MgO, under a company-described 20-year binding MOU; analytical moisture basis undisclosed.
route: Screen/condition residue → acid-based hydrometallurgical recovery of Mg-rich oxide → prepare briquettes with reductant/lime → thermal reduction/refining → intended metal. Demonstrated MgO is an intermediate, not magnesium metal.
capacity_or_output_with_units: FY2026 report specifies initial Phase 1B metal equipment of 500 t/y. The September presentation describes 500 t/y crude crowns followed by 500 t/y refined ingots in Phase 1C: sequential stages of the same metal, not 1,000 t/y combined. The older headline demonstration design of 1,000 t/y is not treated as available capacity. Proposed US first train 50,000 t/y; MgO campaign ~20 t excluded from metal totals.
future_markets: Metal Exchange: future distribution/offtake and prepayment; no proven current metal shipments. US project LOIs: Metal Exchange ≥25,000 t/y, Meridian Lightweight Technologies 5,000 and Twin Cities 2,000; LOIs are not firm realized sales.
gaps: Ash mining/licence arrangements, feed conditioning, financing and commissioning remain dependencies. No verified feed-to-metal ratio. Project forecasts from different releases are not added.

location: Arkansas project at TETRA Evergreen campus; separate San Francisco Bay Area pilot
status: Developer/technical demonstration. The JV operating agreement established Arkansas Magnesium in March 2026; Phase 1 engineering followed. June metal samples from TETRA brine do not establish annual commercial output.
feedstock: Arkansas: TETRA Smackover brine supplies magnesium-bearing chloride. Separately, Cargill agreed to supply San Francisco Bay sea-salt magnesium co-products for pilot scale-up in 2024. These feed chains are distinct. Raw-brine assays, impurity panels and prepared-feed specifications were not located.
route: Prepare and purify brine-derived chloride feed → proprietary electrolysis → refine metal. Product purity above 99.9% is not feed grade.
capacity_or_output_with_units: No verified commercial annual output or operating nameplate. January 2026 announcement targets market placement of up to 7,000 t/y by 2029; a target is not realized output.
future_markets: Wogen’s January agreement covers future distribution from Arkansas Phase 1/2 and working capital. The company also reports pre-sales to an unnamed Detroit Big 3 automaker; no identity or current annual deliveries inferred. Nonbinding demand indications are not production capacity.
gaps: Scale-up, power, feed purification, plant financing and commercial commissioning remain dependencies. JV formation is confirmed; no public feed-to-product ratio located.

location: Budureasa mine/planned smelter; proposed Mother Plant at Beiuș, Bihor, Romania
status: Proposed primary producer backed by sponsor Amerocap. A May 2026 CEO interview describes continuing mine and pilot development, not sustained commercial metal production.
feedstock: Captive Budureasa brucite-bearing ore. The IMA deck claims deposit MgO above 22%; its pilot diagram uses ore at 24.18% MgO and a separated concentrate at 60–69% MgO. Moisture basis and impurities are unspecified. Its T2 illustration shows 11.4 t ore → 3.4 t concentrate → 2.2 t MgO, then 0.8 t aluminum powder added per 1 t metal. This is a company pilot illustration, not verified commercial consumption or a complete mass balance. Aluminum supplier/acceptance grade undisclosed.
route: Separate/upgrade brucite-bearing ore → calcine to oxide → prepare charge with aluminum reductant → aluminothermic reduction → refine/cast metal. Aluminum scrap is intended as a reductant; mineral upgrading is distinct from metal-scrap remelting.
capacity_or_output_with_units: May 2026 CEO interview: 360 t/y Mother Plant followed by up to 30,000 t/y smelter by 2030; quarry restart targeted for end-2026. These are forecasts. The older 90,000 t/y by 2036 ambition is retained only as a historical target, not added capacity.
future_markets: Industrial EU/US markets intended. The May 2026 interview says firm offtake negotiations remain relevant to accelerating the larger smelter; no named binding customer or delivered annual volume verified.
gaps: Financing, resource recertification, permitting, qualification and commissioning remain dependencies. Pilot diagrams do not establish steady-state commercial recovery.

status: Former magnesium site entering municipal redevelopment as 4M2, following insolvency. May 2026 municipal reporting identifies the former Tergeo assets with the new industrial district; an agreement with Exterra supports redevelopment. No commercial primary restart verified.
feedstock: Historical proposal: serpentine tailings for new metal, separate from scrap remelting. The redevelopment page reports access to more than 110 million t of characterized mineral material; this is a stock/resource claim, not magnesium tonnage or annual feed. Assays, prepared chloride purity and future Mg feed rights remain unresolved.
route: Proposed tailings processing → purified magnesium chloride → electrolysis/refining; separate scrap remelting/alloy operations. Recycling startup is not proof that tailings-to-primary-metal production operated commercially.
capacity_or_output_with_units: No reliable current annual primary actual or available nameplate established; pre-insolvency targets excluded from operating capacity.
future_markets: No current offtake or buyer relationship verified after insolvency.
gaps: Municipal redevelopment establishes a new direction for the assets. Exact final asset/title allocation, any future magnesium operator, feed rights and a metal restart schedule remain unverified.

status: Compound-first development by Romanian-owned Mineral Proiect Invest. September 2026 licence is a development milestone. Updated FAQ makes metal only a possible Phase 3, with no selected technology; it is not an operating metal project.
feedstock: Magnesium-bearing serpentinite from the licensed Valea Dobra perimeter near Rășinari; initial crushing at the quarry and planned processing at Săliște. Ore assay, impurities and prepared-feed specifications not located.
route: Initial phases target magnesium oxide, hydroxide and then fused magnesia, all compounds. A possible later metal route remains undecided; Pidgeon is not the process of the proposed Phase 1 compound plant.
capacity_or_output_with_units: No magnesium-metal annual actual or verified operating metal capacity. Compound quantities must not enter metal totals.
future_markets: No named magnesium-metal buyer verified. Compound applications described by the developer do not demonstrate future metal sales.
gaps: Mining, environmental and building approvals are separate. The metal phase remains conditional and must not be treated as licensed or commissioned by the mineral licence alone.

status: Development facility; detailed ownership not disclosed in the reviewed sources. The August 2026 update reports the building completed and major equipment sourced and ordered; first metal is targeted for January 2027. Garrison Minerals is a site partner.
feedstock: DOE describes raw dolomite plus aluminum scrap. Separately, a 2025 Letter of Understanding concerns purchased MgO from Canadian supplier Baymag. These descriptions do not establish the demonstration plant’s final feed mix. Quarry, MgO assay, aluminum-scrap chemistry and preparation losses are undisclosed. Purchased MgO is already an upgraded intermediate, not raw ore.
route: Aluminothermic reduction: prepare magnesium-bearing feed and aluminum reductant → extract and purify magnesium → cast ingot, with calcium aluminate coproduct. This is a thermal chemical-reduction route; electricity use does not make it electrolysis. Detailed feed preparation and current consumption ratios are not disclosed.
capacity_or_output_with_units: No verified commercial annual output. Company pilot results claim magnesium purity above 99.9%. Latest demonstration design: three smelters totaling at least 200 tons/year, with “tons” left undefined by the company; not converted to metric tonnes. DOE’s 2,000-hour continuous-run objective is a future demonstration target. Calcium aluminate is excluded from magnesium-metal quantities.
future_markets: No named magnesium customer or delivered customer tonnage located in the reviewed disclosures. Baymag is an input supplier and Garrison a site partner; neither relationship establishes a magnesium-metal purchase. DOE identifies potential alloying, lightweight-part and metallurgical uses, not contracted buyers.
gaps: Commissioning, sustained recovery, energy/reductant consumption, consistent product qualification and customer commitments remain to be demonstrated. Final feed contracts and permitted commercial operating conditions were not established by the reviewed announcements.
